entries:
Alpha 1.4.0 (the Fourfold Chronicle)

  • Meet the people behind the diaries: Mara Fen, Dain, Hessa and Selen now live in Lanternhold’s open southern plaza. Approach and speak to them for optional conversations about the lives the crystals protect.
  • Sixteen conversations to uncover: Ask about shelter, promises, shared warmth and the freedom to choose. Further topics open as you record each witness’s field evidence and complete their realm’s crystal restoration. No quest or reward is automatically claimed.
  • The world answers your work: After a crystal’s quest is turned in, its investigation landmarks show new growth, renewed crossing cloths and ripples, warm hearths and pottery, or wind-filled pennants. These personal changes preserve the old ruins, open walking routes and shared-world hazards.
  • After the Vigil: Four new journal epilogues explain what restoration means to the people of each realm. Open pages and dialogue topics stay put during quest updates, with readable phone controls.
  • Ilyra still guides the Chronicle: The existing eight investigations, manual quest handoffs, four dungeon roads, full raid and crystal-defense requirements, resonance portal and Dark King conclusion remain intact. Witnesses are not daily quest givers, and existing progress and rewards are preserved.

Alpha 1.3.0 (combat with impact)

  • Aim with your thumb: Drag the phone skill button or an assigned hotbar skill to preview direction and range, then release to cast. Slide back to cancel. Taps keep selected-target behavior; self and ally skills keep their own targeting.
  • Reliable self buffs: Caster-centered skills and personal buffs no longer try to approach a selected enemy or turn toward the cursor before casting. Aimed charges and ally-targeted heals retain their targeting rules.
  • Know when you can cast: The target card shows cooldown or missing mana while keeping range and safe-zone warnings first. Failed casts explain the wait or exact mana shortage.
  • Feel each class: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard and Cleric have distinct local cast sounds and refined attack windup and follow-through. Short actions blend in faster without changing attack speed or damage timing.
  • Your camera, your comfort: Optional camera impacts respond to your direct combat hits and landings, not other players jumping. Adjust saved impact strength from zero to full; motion stays off by default and respects device reduced-motion settings.
  • Warnings that stand out: Dark-backed danger edges stay readable on bright ground at both graphics settings, with the same damage boundary. Nearby party hit effects are more compact without reducing your effects or hazard warnings.
  • Combat rules stay grounded: Existing server targeting, dungeon wall checks, cooldowns, mana costs, gear stats and rewards remain in force. No level-based stat multiplier has been added.

Alpha 1.2.0 (heroes worth looking at)

  • Hero refinement: Smoother exposed faces and visible hands improve the four-class models. Hands remain in place when gloves and weapons change.
  • Natural strides: Heroes lean forward when running, with smoother walking and running motion and articulated boots. Equipped footwear follows the same ankle motion. Movement speed and attack timing are unchanged.
  • Controls for your hands: Phone settings now offer left- or right-handed combat controls and independently saved touch sizing. Camera framing follows the layout; very short landscape screens keep standard control size to preserve viewing space.
  • Your camera, remembered: Phone and desktop camera zoom save independently of each other and of menu text size.
  • A readable Forge: Phone equipment lists show names, level and potency in large rows, with larger controls and collapsible forging help. Selected equipment continues to refresh after upgrades.
  • A clearer Trading House: Named inventory rows show quantities and selection. Phone selling forms and auction controls are larger, and expandable item details work without hovering.
  • Community on your phone: Social, friend and guild lists use readable cards. Guild management actions sit under Manage, and PvP challenges, results and leaderboards have readable text and touch-sized controls.
  • Explore the map by touch: Drag to pan, pinch to zoom, or use the zoom and Find me buttons. Phone labels remain readable as you zoom, and the map fits portrait and landscape screens.

Alpha 1.1.0 (a dependable adventure)

  • Dungeon combat and travel: Improved boss encounters, attack targeting, dungeon-wall checks and return-to-town recovery. The first dungeon includes optional preparation tips for equipment, party roles and town rest.
  • Party progression: A four-role party can clear Verdant Bastion and individually claim Ilyra's chapter reward and next-realm offer. A teammate's turn-in does not complete your quest for you.
  • Training that works: Corrected Fighter, Rogue and Cleric talent effects, including area, duration, damage and utility bonuses. Resolve, Zeal and Mark Masteries strengthen their actual bonuses, with matching offline effects and readable buff details.
  • Clearer attacks and protection: Earthshaker and other area effects show their resolved boundaries. Blade Storm and Tripwire respect dungeon walls. Iron Fortress and Guardian Roar consistently apply their damage protection.
  • More reliable controls: Healing under overlapping enemies no longer accidentally selects a hostile target. Desktop talent purchases wait for confirmation and recover from rejection or reconnect. Expandable menu sections retain normal keyboard behavior.
  • Character and equipment consistency: Improved equipped-item and character presentation. Removing health equipment clamps health to the new maximum without refilling health or mana.
  • Phone adventure: Improved phone camera framing, touch targeting and readable menu layouts, including inventory, quests, skills and party support. Further visual and ergonomic refinement continues in 1.2.
  • Arena reliability: Corrected practice/duel reward handling and team-elimination behavior, and fixed delayed attacks overlapping an arena return.
  • Alpha development: Milestone releases continue with focused checks and live smoke tests. The exhaustive cross-game balancing and compatibility pass is reserved for final full-feature stabilization.

Alpha 1.0.65 (training that shapes your magic)

  • A stronger Focus charge: Spell Focus Mastery improves the stored next-damage-spell multiplier. Utility casts preserve that charge, and the displayed bonus agrees with the server.
  • Time Warp Mastery lasts longer: Each rank extends this support spell's duration instead of promising damage it never deals. Duration training and the equipped set continue to work together.
  • Teleport obeys the battlefield: Warp bursts use trained damage and area, respect dungeon walls, and show their departure and arrival boundaries. Offline Teleport uses the canonical landing height, Phase immunity and Temporal Weave recharge rules.
  • Protection you can read: A timed Protected status and light orbital effect show temporary immunity without enclosing the character in a glowing box. The effect clears on expiry, death and respawn.
  • Consistent offline spell training: Wizard damage spells use their own Mastery and base damage profiles. Focus is captured once for the next damage spell; stun does not prolong Phase or pause Teleport recharge.
  • The same progression: Quest rewards, manual turn-ins, town recovery and Well Rested remain unchanged. This update does not declare the full dungeon or balance pass complete.
  • Independent rehearsal checks: Non-deploying branch checks no longer wait behind the production release queue. Production releases remain serialized and retain their native-browser acceptance checks.
  • A cleaner phone status panel: The reading surface is now opaque, so buttons and bright effects behind it do not show through descriptions. Its compact size and reachable combat controls are unchanged.

Alpha 1.0.64 (defenses you can depend on)

  • Protection across combat: Direct abilities, projectiles, lingering areas, summons, poison and bleeding now respect receiving defenses, including Arcane Shield, Sanctuary and temporary invulnerability. Basic attacks apply outgoing damage bonuses before those defenses.
  • Shields end cleanly: Expired shields cannot absorb or retaliate between updates. Reflective shields strike the actual attacker, and depletion cannot clear a newly recast shield.
  • Explosions respect the battlefield: Explosive Arcane Shields respect dungeon walls, party protection and valid PvP opponents. Their blasts observe defensive effects and PvP limits, including when another shield explodes in response. Equipment's on-kill explosions also respect walls and their circular reach, retain enemy-only targeting, and generate threat from the damage dealt.
  • Consistent wounds: Poison and bleed budgets apply their outgoing bonuses and PvP limits once per recipient. Raw wounds honor critical training and equipment effects; wounds inherited from an earlier hit do not apply those bonuses again.
  • Progression stays familiar: Existing quest rewards, manual turn-ins, town recovery and Well Rested are unchanged. The wider dungeon and progression acceptance work continues.

Alpha 1.0.63 (a clearer spell of support)

  • Time Warp reaches its trained area: Area talents now extend the allies reached by Time Warp. The caster-centered effect agrees with that reach for the caster and other players at both graphics quality settings.
  • Consistent offline haste: Time Warp uses its trained duration and cooldown, updates movement and attack speed correctly, and removes its bonuses when it expires—even while stunned. Its six-piece set effect retains its zone-wide reach.
  • A dependable Spell Focus charge: Offline Spell Focus respects duration and cooldown training, survives utility casts such as Teleport, correctly empowers the next Fireball, and expires normally. Locked or rejected casts do not spend the charge.
  • Build menus recover from rejection: Talent, specialization and rune controls no longer stay stuck waiting when the server rejects a change. A rejected purchase does not spend points or retry itself.
  • Clearer release evidence: Live animation checks retain separate reports for each class and multiplayer stage.

Alpha 1.0.62 (adventure together)

  • Party kill credit: Connected party members in the same dungeon or raid share kill credit throughout the instance, including downed teammates. Overworld parties share nearby kill rewards within roughly two normal screens. Credit is recorded when the enemy dies; each player still returns to the quest giver to complete their quests.
  • Dependable crowd control: Stunned enemies stop moving and cannot finish an ordinary attack while stunned. Roots stop movement, slows expire correctly, and other players see these effects consistently. Boss immunity remains intact.
  • Clearer party healing: A compact desktop roster keeps four teammates' names, health and healing targets together. Explicit support targets are validated before spending mana; party reward guidance explains who qualifies.
  • Equipment stays current: Forge and item details refresh after upgrades without reopening the window. Socketed gems use consistent colors in item icons and equipped gear, with improved held-weapon clearance.
  • Smoother rested effects: Well Rested's aura uses shared rendering resources to reduce repeated work around groups. Town recovery, rested bonuses and the two-hour duration limit are unchanged.
  • More reliable combat controls: Move-only input avoids accidental attacks. Guardian Roar and Executioner Spin use their trained areas, while Purifying Wave's Mastery improves its cleansing area.
  • Keep the adventure moving: Ready story objectives give clearer guidance to return to Ilyra. New characters begin with an empty personal stash; existing saved belongings and character stats are preserved.

Alpha 1.0.61 (a new home for Eidolon)

  • A new address: Play at play.eidolonrealms.com, with secure game connections to server.eidolonrealms.com.
  • Your adventure carries over: Existing accounts and characters use the same server and database. The new site may ask you to log in again; browser-local settings and cached assets belong to each site separately.
  • Safer release delivery: Queued deployments now use the exact commit that passed their checks, even when newer changes arrive while they wait.
  • No balance changes: This migration does not change combat, town recovery, Well Rested, quests, loot or progression.

Alpha 1.0.60 (beyond the sanctuary)

  • Know when safety blocks combat: Online enemy target cards now say "Leave the safe zone" while town protection prevents PvE damage, instead of suggesting that range alone makes the attack usable. The warning appears on desktop and phone.
  • Clear feedback on departure: Normal range feedback returns when the server confirms that you have left the safe zone, including when you keep the same enemy targeted.
  • Duel rules stay intact: The new PvE warning does not replace feedback for a valid player-versus-player duel target.
  • The same recovery and progression: This feedback correction does not change town healing, Well Rested, casting, mana costs, damage, quest rewards, drop rates or story requirements.
